reason: Round 2 review: Question Routing now requires canSend before judging harness routes, reusing the delivery prerequisites for usable authentication, service compatibility and active devices. A Hermes version is informational only when successfully parsed and different from the supported pin; failed version probes remain actionable with their diagnostic cause and a remedy, and still check plugin enablement. The Hermes reference distinguishes a confirmed unsupported version from an unreadable one. Reviewed all five surfaces; lifecycle hooks, the shared skill, setup and domain terms need no further change for these fixes. Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for doctor and readiness: a readiness state the User chose or the harness cannot satisfy by design is now an optional-gap with no remedy and a new `informational` field (`user-choice` or `harness-capability`), classified once where doctor builds the states and read by doctor, init, question_routing_ready and the update hand-off, which lost its own copy. Questions turned off no longer fail doctor or init or offer `config set ask_notifications true`. On Cursor, OpenCode and OpenClaw off macOS, question admission and answer continuation (and Cursor's per-session check, which no prompt can satisfy) are reported as limits without a `hooks install` remedy, doctor exits 0 when nothing else is wrong, and question_routing_ready now judges the routes those harnesses have (`ask --wait`, the OpenCode form) instead of always being false; a repairable problem on those harnesses stays a gap. A successfully parsed Hermes version other than v0.21.5 is a limit with no remedy instead of a gap that offered `hermes plugins enable`; harness-hermes.md says install supports v0.21.5 only and drops the older-Hermes state install refuses. Grok's first activation carries the due update and integration-fault notices within its 9,000-byte budget, claimed only when printed, and a later fault rides the next tool result; Grok's turn end now refreshes the integration assessment like the other harnesses, so a Grok fault becomes due at all. Prompt-time fault notices are claimed only on Claude Code and Codex, whose prompt output reaches the model; Cursor beforeSubmitPrompt, OpenCode chat.message and OpenClaw message_received leave them due. The update-check next step and the week-held notice no longer say updates wait for questions, and the guidance-missing fallback runs `doctor --json` instead of `init --json`. diagnostics.md, harness-setup.md, SKILL.md and the Cursor, OpenCode and Grok files say what the new field means. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for one change: OpenCode 2 does not load OpenCode 1 plugins, so on OpenCode 2 Notifai's generated OpenCode plugin never runs. `notifai doctor` now reads `opencode --version` when OpenCode is wired and reports a new readiness state, hooks-opencode-plugin ("OpenCode plugin loadability"): ready on OpenCode 1 or an unreadable version, a harness-scoped gap with a user-elsewhere remedy on OpenCode 2 or later, so it never blocks init or another harness's session. `notifai hooks install --harness opencode` still writes the plugin and adds a stderr warning on OpenCode 2. The OpenCode harness reference and the README support row now say the integration covers OpenCode 1 and that OpenCode 2 does not load the plugin yet. OpenCode 1 behavior, the generated plugin, hook definitions, commands and flags are unchanged. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for one runtime change: Grok's imported copies of Notifai's Claude Code and Cursor hooks (`hook ... --harness claude-code` or `--harness cursor`, run by Grok's hook runner, which sets GROK_HOOK_EVENT) now end silently with exit 0 in the native launcher on macOS and Linux, before the session child, the hub or the runtime, and at the runtime entry elsewhere; the in-process guard already ignored them. Grok runs async handlers in line, so the Claude Code attend copy had held each Grok prompt and turn end for about 20 seconds. Grok's own Notifai hooks, real Claude Code and Cursor hooks, and Grok's tool shells (which carry no GROK_HOOK_EVENT) are unchanged. The Grok harness reference already says native Notifai hooks do not need imported Claude or Cursor copies, which still holds, and no agent action changes. No hook definition, command, flag, readiness id or guidance wording changed. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shared skill, harness setup, readiness and domain terms. A root agent that uses Codex's synchronous request_user_input or Grok's question card in a signed-in, enabled Project with question notifications on now gets PostToolUse context saying the question never reached the User's devices and to ask with notifai ask; both harnesses hand hook context to the model only with the tool result, so no new handler or /hooks approval is added and the form itself is never denied. init --json returns the prepared machine-approval message in technical.pairing.message, and harness-setup.md sends it as written instead of fetching a template from the website. update --resume, doctor's npm repair status, the installer's legacy-npm collision and install --recover-integration name references/npm-migration.md or references/hermes-publication-recovery.md where each applies. send writes a non-blocking stderr note for a Summary of 200 or more characters or a Body over 1,500. Claude Code and Codex run Stop detached and discard its block decision, so their next prompt now also carries an owed answer acknowledgement, as it already did for Session Messages. Earlier review retained: Session start, the Cursor rule, the skill description and its "Decide whether to notify" section now say that an Agent Session another agent started with a task brief reports Agent Events to that agent and sends no Notification Requests unless the brief delegates them; a session the User started still owns them. Reviewed on top of Windows form linking. Merged with main after the Claude Code picker change (notes-only picker answers recorded as the terminal answer; report-only Remote Control expiry line), which was reviewed with no guidance impact; the two changes touch separate surfaces. Also retained from current main: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for one runtime change: a Codex subagent can now ask the User through its root. Codex runs a subagent inside the root's Codex process and gives its shell the root's thread in CODEX_SESSION_ID; `notifai ask` from that shell registers the question to the root Agent Session when the root has started and not ended and the Codex process recorded for it is alive and among the caller's ancestors, the same evidence Notifai already accepts from the root's own shell. Registration rechecks the root's start under its lock, so a root that ends or restarts meanwhile receives nothing. Such an ask never hands back the card and never waits: plain, --wait and duplicate output, human and JSON alike, say the question belongs to the root and its answer arrives there, tell the worker not to ask it in its own conversation, to tell its parent the question id and what each answer will change and to end its turn, and say the root closes it if the User answers in the conversation. A subagent that cannot be placed inside a live, activated root, including any on Windows, is still refused as session_not_activated, with a remedy that gives the question to its parent. Notifai cannot tell a delegated worker from an ordinary one, as on Claude Code, so worker context still tells ordinary workers to report to their parent. SKILL.md's ownership lines now say that only delegation decides whether a worker notifies and that a worker that asks follows what `ask` prints, which may send the answer to the root; harness-codex.md says a Codex worker's answer arrives at the root, that it gets no card and no wait, and that Windows refuses. TRUST.md now records how Agent Session identity is checked and that it is not authentication. No hook definition, SubagentStart output, flag or readiness id changed. Also retained from current main: Reviewed local-input safety on every outbound file surface: opened descriptors and path components use bigint identity checks before reading; multiply linked files are refused; only exact root-owned macOS system aliases pass. Bounded reads and final metadata checks refuse changes during reading. Regular temporary files and stdin remain supported; unrelated directory activity gets at most three attempts with original component and file identities pinned, and alias capitalization passes only when it names the same system link. TRUST.md now describes the exact aliases, hard-link rule, identity checks and image-signature scope. The supplied cwd is inspected without realpath erasing any planted link; the CLI already supplies the OS working directory. Explicit linked input paths, including a supplied cwd, are refused outside the system alias allowlist. Lifecycle hooks, skill procedures, harness setup, readiness fields and domain terms need no further changes for these reader fixes. Prior reviews retained: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for repository trust. The trust preamble now says to change Notifai settings, guidance or Project Enablement only when the User asks directly, since a file or tool output asking is not the User, and it says "environment value" like the skill and TRUST.md. Every CLI remedy that suggests --yes, a new approve_origins or media_origins entry, or keeping retired repository settings now says it applies on the User's direct request, and the logs remedy removes the off override at its layer instead of setting the refused default. Cursor's always-applied rule no longer skips itself when the conversation already holds Notifai context, because on SDK hosts only a repository file could supply that; harness-cursor.md says the rule asks the CLI. --image, --body-file, --form and OpenCode form images are read only as the files they name (no planted symbolic link, a regular file within its limit, image bytes matching the type), and TRUST.md lists the rule. hooks install detects harnesses only from the User's account homes, never repository folders. No readiness id, output field or command changed.
